messages:
sam: Heads up — bringing up an HF model (gpt-style) via the conversion tool and seeing a nasty quality/regression after int4 quant. conversion log flagged mismatches in config.json: rope_scaling, sliding_window, num_key_value_heads, max_position_embeddings. anyone seen this stack before? :eyes:

lee: yep. had a case where sliding_window was absent and our runtime assumed default true -> kv cache offsets got shifted. short prompts looked fine, long convo collapsed.

mira: can you paste the HF config snippet? sometimes rope_scaling formats differ (dict vs float) and we ignore it which shifts position math.

sam: pasted below (from the model repo):
```json
{
  "max_position_embeddings": 8192,
  "num_key_value_heads": 16,
  "rope_scaling": {"type":"linear","factor":0.8},
  "sliding_window": true
}
```

lee: ok two immediate red flags: 1) num_key_value_heads vs attention heads ratio not validated; 2) sliding_window:true plus rope_scaling non-identity -> our conversion used default max_pos trimming which mismatched kv cache size.

raj: add to that: in quantized kernels we assume kv head layout N,K,H where K computed from max_position_embeddings. If max_pos larger than runtime clip, the cache address math wraps. results look like attention focusing on recent tokens only (quality drop).

anya: small repro I run: convert + int4 quant -> run zero-shot on PALMS benchmark set. with sliding_window true i get 12% BLEU drop vs false. with rope_scaling removed it's within 2%.

mira: quick mitigation options:
- clamp max_position_embeddings to runtime supported (e.g., 4096) during conversion
- if rope_scaling is non-default, force explicit position interpolation path in runtime
- if num_key_value_heads present, validate equals attention_heads or apply head mapping rule and emit warning

sam: could we add a conversion sanity-check that emits a failing warning and a conversion-adjusted config? Right now converter quietly writes the fields and runtime assumes defaults.

lee: yeah. suggested diff for converter: if sliding_window missing -> set false and add note; if rope_scaling is dict -> copy verbatim to "rope_scaling_raw" and create normalized float factor for runtime compatibility. Also validate kv heads mapping: if num_key_value_heads != attention_head_count and num_attention_heads % num_key_value_heads != 0 -> fail.

mira: repro script i used (quick):
```bash
python tools/convert_hf.py --model ./hf-model --out ./converted --clamp-max-pos 4096 --warn-kv-heads
python infra/eval.py --model ./converted --quant int4 --prompts small_eval_set.jsonl
```
results attached in thread artifacts.

deploy-bot: conversion job #287 completed: s3://redwood-convs/1854321987/artifacts/ (logs + converted/config.json) :white_check_mark:

raj: we should also add a unit test in eng-ml that fuzzes rope_scaling and sliding_window combos with quant paths. most regressions only surface under int4.

anya: agreed. i can add a small harness that runs 50 short convos and checks perplexity delta < 5% after conversion/quant.

sam: quick triage outcome: patched converter to clamp max_position_embeddings -> 4096, emit kv-head mismatch fatal error, and if rope_scaling is a dict we translate to runtime-friendly linear factor when possible. reran quantized evals — quality returned to baseline. i'll open PR with changelog and link tests. :thumbsup:

lee: awesome. also file a follow-up to check chat templates: some templates assumed global max_pos and we need to guard template truncation with converted max_pos.

mira: noted, will add to checklist.

sam: thanks all. will post PR link once CI passes.

deploy-bot: PR #874 opened by sam: https://git.internal/redwood/convertor/pulls/874 (conversion: clamp-max-pos, kv-head-validation, rope_scaling normalization)

lee: reviewed quickly, left minor comments.

sam: merging after fixes.

anya: follow-up task: add a small doc in onboarding checklist "HF -> Redwood gotchas: rope_scaling, sliding_window, kv_heads, max_pos" with repro snippets. i'll draft.

sam: perfect. closing thread when PR merged. :white_check_mark:
